definitions: A class in object-oriented programming that encapsulates a primitive data type or another object, providing additional functionality or allowing it to be treated as an object.
In Java, a class that provides a way to use primitive data types (like int, char, boolean) as objects, enabling them to be stored in collections or passed to methods that expect objects.
examples: The Integer wrapper class name allows an int to be used in a List.
Autoboxing automatically converts a primitive to its wrapper class name.
Each primitive type has a corresponding wrapper class name.
